items.justification: Consented automatic updating on a device versus preview access that lets operators evaluate model changes.
Timely action on disclosed vulnerabilities versus AI content in a training programme.
Per-device password uniqueness versus secure coding training.
Updateability of software components versus disaster recovery planning.
User guidance on checking secure setup versus security testing before release.
Both concern getting fixes onto the deployed product, A through an automatable mechanism, B through the supply and delivery obligation.
Vulnerability disclosure policy versus separation of development environments.
Both examine operational data for security-relevant anomalies, A in device telemetry, B in model behaviour over time.
Technical updateability of components versus the obligation to notify users of updates.
Both protect confidential material held at rest, A security parameters in device storage, B training data and model weights.
Prompt patching and mitigation where patching is impossible are the two arms of managing known vulnerabilities.
Both address products that cannot be updated; A names isolation, B requires mechanisms and contingency plans generally, of which isolation is one.
Cryptographic strength of authentication versus an organizational access control review.
Acting on disclosed vulnerabilities and planning for the unpatchable case cover the two outcomes of a vulnerability report.
Encryption of sensitive personal data versus interpretability of model outputs.
Both require ongoing observation to surface security problems, A of the product, B of the model's internal states.
Authentication before configuration change versus accessible user guidance.
Orderly network reconnection versus evaluating outputs for reverse engineering risk.
Encryption of sensitive personal data versus threat modelling on configuration change.
Orderly network reconnection versus transparency about data use and storage.
Finding and fixing vulnerabilities and supporting affected users through an incident are separate parts of one response capability.
Internal monitoring and rectification and a published disclosure route are the inward and outward halves of vulnerability management.
Secure storage of security parameters versus publishing a vulnerability disclosure policy.
Both govern how software change is handled safely, A by requiring components to be securely updateable, B by re-testing after a major change.
Cryptographic protection of the update path and secure supply chain process together establish that delivered software is trustworthy.
Ease of applying an update versus sanitisation of data and inputs.
Cryptography for secure communication versus an organizational access control review.
Usability of installation and maintenance versus secure software supply chain processes.
Hardware memory access control versus maintaining an asset inventory.
Alerting on detected software tampering versus documenting public training data provenance.
Cryptography for secure communication versus sharing documentation with End-users.
Ease of applying an update versus an audit log of configuration changes.
A secure development process and design-time sanitisation of data and inputs are distinct obligations within secure engineering of the artefact.
Password uniqueness versus guidance on appropriate use and failure modes.
Both harden a remotely accessible interface, A by protecting the credentials it carries, B by limiting how it can be exercised.
Instructions for deleting personal data versus publishing a vulnerability disclosure policy.
A secure development process relies on staff raising risks they notice, which is what B mandates.
Publishing the rationale for absent updates versus due diligence on external components.
Usability of installation and maintenance versus secure deletion at decommissioning.
Authentication before configuration change versus the patch delivery chain.
